This Executive Summary alone does not constitute a complete Phase I Environmental Site Assessment under ASTM E1527-21 or 40 CFR Part 312.

**[1. Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**

Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC (\"Clearfield\") was retained by Calverley Heritage Bank (\"CHB\" or \"User\") to conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") of the property located at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403 (the \"Subject Property\"). The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to identify Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"RECs\"), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") in connection with the Subject Property, as those terms are defined in ASTM E1527-21, Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process.

This assessment was conducted to support a proposed commercial real estate loan from Calverley Heritage Bank to Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC in connection with the acquisition and renovation of the Subject Property. Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC has been designated as an additional user of and intended reliance party for this report with the prior written consent of Clearfield.

The Phase I ESA was conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 and is intended to satisfy the \"All Appropriate Inquiries\" (\"AAI\") standard under 40 CFR Part 312, thereby qualifying the User for the innocent landowner, contiguous property owner, and bona fide prospective purchaser defenses to liability under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. §§ 9601 *et seq.*

The scope of services performed in connection with this Phase I ESA included the following:

> • Review of federal, state, tribal, and local environmental regulatory database records, including standard and additional databases as specified by ASTM E1527-21;
>
> • Historical use review utilizing aerial photographs (reviewed from 1938 to present), Sanborn fire insurance maps, city directories, and building department records obtained from the City of Charleston Department of Planning, Preservation and Sustainability;
>
> • Site reconnaissance, conducted on January 15, 2025, including an interior and exterior inspection of the Subject Property and visual observation of adjoining properties from the Subject Property boundaries;
>
> • Interviews with the current property owner, current occupants, and local government officials with knowledge of the Subject Property and surrounding area; and
>
> • Evaluation of adjoining and nearby properties for conditions that may affect the Subject Property.

**Limitations:** This assessment did not include the sampling or analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, or building materials. No Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (subsurface investigation) was conducted as part of this engagement. The findings and conclusions set forth herein are based solely on non-invasive methods.

**Data Gaps:** No significant data gaps were identified during the course of this assessment. Historical records were available for the Subject Property from 1938 to the present, and regulatory database searches returned complete results for all standard search distances.

**[2. Subject Property Description]{.underline}**

**Address:** 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403

**Legal Description:** Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, in the Register of Mesne Conveyances (\"RMC\") Office for Charleston County, South Carolina; together with that certain strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, conveyed to the predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**Tax Map Numbers:** 460-12-04-007 (Lot 7), 460-12-04-008 (Lot 8), and 460-12-04-009 (Lot 9)

**Total Land Area:** Approximately 0.38 acres (approximately 16,553 square feet)

**Improvements:** The Subject Property is improved with a mixed-use commercial building consisting of ground-floor retail space (three bays totaling approximately 11,400 square feet) and upper-floor office space (two stories, approximately 19,600 square feet), for a total gross building area of approximately 31,000 square feet. The building features a masonry and steel-frame construction with a flat membrane roof, which was last replaced in 2017 according to building department records.

**Year Built:** The original commercial structure was constructed in 1952. A significant renovation was completed in 2004, converting the upper floors from storage and warehouse use to Class B office space and upgrading building systems including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire suppression.

**Current Use:** Mixed-use retail and office, as follows:

> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 1** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 7): Occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc., a specialty grocery retailer.
>
> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 2** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 8): Currently vacant.
>
> • **Ground Floor --- Bay 3** (approximately 3,800 SF; Lot 9): Occupied by Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC, an interior design firm.
>
> • **Second Floor --- Suite A** (approximately 9,800 SF): Occupied by Tidemark Consulting Group LLC, a management consulting firm.
>
> • **Second Floor --- Suite B** (approximately 9,800 SF): Currently vacant.

**Physical Description of Lots:** Lot 7 is the southwestern parcel, fronting King Street, containing Bay 1 on the ground floor and a portion of the second-floor area. Lot 8 is the central parcel containing Bay 2 and additional second-floor area. Lot 9 is the northeastern parcel containing Bay 3 and the remainder of the second floor. The former Anson Lane strip runs along the rear (northwest) boundary of Lots 7, 8, and 9 and currently provides rear access and loading for the building.

**Zoning:** GB (General Business), City of Charleston.

**Topography:** The Subject Property is generally flat with minimal grade change across the site. The Subject Property is situated in FEMA Flood Zone X (area of minimal flood hazard) based on FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map Panel No. 45019C0520J, effective December 4, 2020.

**Utilities:** Public water and sewer service is provided by the Charleston Water System. Electrical service is provided by South Carolina Electric & Gas. An easement for underground utility lines across the rear of the Subject Property is recorded in Deed Book 987 at Page 112, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**[3. Historical Use Summary]{.underline}**

The following historical use summary is based on Clearfield\'s review of Sanborn fire insurance maps (1902, 1919, 1944, 1955, 1970, and 1989 editions), aerial photographs (reviewed at approximately five-year intervals from 1938 to present), city directories (1948 through 2024), and building department records obtained from the City of Charleston.

**Subject Property Historical Uses:**

**Pre-1952:** The Subject Property was part of the Hampstead Village residential neighborhood. Lots 7, 8, and 9 were each improved with single-family wood-frame residences, consistent with the surrounding residential character of the area as depicted on Sanborn maps and aerial photographs from this period. Anson Lane was a public alley running behind the lots, providing rear access to the residences and adjacent properties.

**1952:** The single-family residences on Lots 7, 8, and 9 were demolished and the original commercial structure was constructed across all three lots. Building department records indicate the structure was initially built for general retail purposes. The 1955 Sanborn map depicts the building as a one-story commercial structure with a partial second-story storage area.

**1952--2003:** The Subject Property was in continuous use for general retail and small commercial office purposes. City directory listings and building department records from this period identify various tenants, including a hardware store (approximately 1956--1971), a clothing retailer (approximately 1972--1989), and miscellaneous small office and retail tenants thereafter. No evidence of hazardous substance use, storage, treatment, or disposal on the Subject Property was identified during this period. No underground storage tanks or above-ground storage tanks were identified in association with any tenant or use during this period.

**2004:** A significant renovation converted the upper floors from storage and warehouse use to Class B office space. Building systems, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire suppression, were upgraded. Building department permits and inspection records from the 2004 renovation do not reference any environmental incidents, the discovery of contaminated materials, or the removal of underground storage tanks.

**2019:** City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 vacated the public alley formerly known as Anson Lane. The vacated strip was conveyed to the then-owner of the Subject Property by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, RMC Office for Charleston County.

**2004--Present:** The Subject Property has been in continuous mixed-use retail and office occupancy, consistent with its current configuration.

**Adjacent Property Historical Use --- 518 King Street:**

The property located at 518 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina (immediately southwest of and adjoining Lot 7 of the Subject Property) is of particular significance to this assessment. Based on city directory listings, building department records, and Sanborn map review, 518 King Street was historically operated as a dry cleaning establishment known as \"King Street Cleaners\" from approximately 1968 through 2005. Dry cleaning operations at this location involved the use of perchloroethylene (\"PCE,\" also known as tetrachloroethylene) and other petroleum-based solvents. The dry cleaning facility was closed in 2005, and the building at 518 King Street was subsequently converted to a restaurant, which remains its current use. Environmental contamination associated with the former dry cleaning operation at 518 King Street is discussed in detail in Section 5 below.

**[4. Findings --- Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)]{.underline}**

**No Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs) were identified in connection with the Subject Property.**

Clearfield reviewed applicable federal and state environmental regulatory databases in accordance with ASTM E1527-21 search distance requirements, including: the EPA National Priorities List (\"NPL\"); the CERCLIS/SEMS database; the RCRA Corrective Action (CORRACTS) and Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF) lists; the RCRA generators lists (large and small quantity generators); the Emergency Response Notification System (\"ERNS\"); state-equivalent hazardous waste site and solid waste facility lists; the Leaking Underground Storage Tank (\"LUST\") and Underground Storage Tank (\"UST\") databases maintained by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (\"SCDHEC\"); SCDHEC Voluntary Cleanup Program records; SCDHEC Brownfields Program sites; and state spill and release notification databases.

The Subject Property does not appear on any federal or state environmental database as a site of concern, listed facility, generator, or location of a reported release.

During the site reconnaissance conducted on January 15, 2025, no evidence of underground storage tanks, above-ground storage tanks, or hazardous substance storage was observed on the Subject Property or identified in historical records. No evidence of staining, stressed vegetation, illegal dumping, waste disposal, or other indicators of releases or threatened releases of hazardous substances or petroleum products was observed on the Subject Property.

**No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs) were identified in connection with the Subject Property.**

**One (1) Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) was identified in connection with the Subject Property**, as described in detail in Section 5 below.

**[5. Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (CREC) --- Lot 7]{.underline}**

**5.1 Background and Source of Contamination**

A Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition (\"CREC\"), as defined by ASTM E1527-21, was identified with respect to Lot 7 of the Subject Property (Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007). A CREC is defined under ASTM E1527-21 as a recognized environmental condition resulting from a past release of hazardous substances or petroleum products that has been addressed to the satisfaction of the applicable regulatory authority, with hazardous substances or petroleum products allowed to remain in place subject to the implementation of required controls.

The CREC arises from off-site contamination originating at the adjacent property located at 518 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, which is immediately southwest of and adjoining Lot 7. As described in Section 3 above, 518 King Street was formerly operated as \"King Street Cleaners,\" a dry cleaning establishment, from approximately 1968 to 2005.

Operations at King Street Cleaners involved the use of perchloroethylene (\"PCE,\" also known as tetrachloroethylene) and petroleum-based solvents in commercial dry cleaning equipment. A release of PCE and petroleum-based solvents from the former dry cleaning operation resulted in subsurface soil and shallow groundwater contamination that migrated off-site in a generally northeastern direction --- consistent with the local shallow groundwater flow gradient --- toward and into the southwest corner of Lot 7 of the Subject Property.

The contamination was identified, reported to the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control (\"SCDHEC\"), and assigned SCDHEC Site Identification Number SC-29403-0772. The SCDHEC file for this site documents the nature and extent of contamination, the remediation activities undertaken, and the regulatory determination described below.

**5.2 Remediation and Regulatory Closure**

Remediation activities were conducted at the source area on the 518 King Street property and at the impacted portion of Lot 7 of the Subject Property under SCDHEC oversight. Remediation included excavation and off-site disposal of impacted soils, in-situ chemical oxidation treatment of residual soil and groundwater contamination, and a multi-year program of groundwater and soil vapor monitoring to assess the effectiveness of remedial activities.

Following the completion of remedial activities and a period of post-remediation monitoring demonstrating stable or declining contaminant concentrations, SCDHEC issued a \"No Further Action\" (\"NFA\") letter dated August 12, 2021, for SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772. The NFA letter concluded that residual contamination levels in soil and groundwater at and beneath the southwest corner of Lot 7 had been reduced to levels protective of human health and the environment under a commercial and non-residential use scenario, subject to certain institutional controls.

**Important:** The NFA letter was issued subject to conditions --- specifically, the implementation and maintenance of the institutional controls described in Section 5.3 below. The NFA status is contingent upon continued compliance with these institutional controls. A failure to maintain the required institutional controls could result in SCDHEC reopening the site for additional investigation, remediation, or regulatory action.

**5.3 Institutional Controls --- Recorded Land Use Restriction**

As a condition of the SCDHEC NFA determination for Site ID SC-29403-0772, a Land Use Restriction (\"LUR\") was recorded against Lot 7 of the Subject Property in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, at Deed Book 1203 at Page 89. The recorded LUR imposes two specific obligations that run with the land and are binding upon all current and future owners, tenants, lessees, successors, and assigns of Lot 7:

> **(a) Prohibition on Residential Use.** The ground floor of Lot 7 --- that is, Bay 1 of the Subject Property, comprising approximately 3,800 square feet and currently occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery --- shall not be converted to or used for residential purposes. This restriction is intended to prevent exposure pathways associated with continuous residential indoor occupancy, including potential vapor intrusion of residual volatile organic compounds (\"VOCs\") from subsurface soil and groundwater into the indoor air of Bay 1 at levels that may exceed residential screening criteria.
>
> **(b) Vapor Barrier Maintenance Obligation.** The property owner is required to maintain, in good condition and working order, a vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1 (Lot 7, ground floor). The vapor barrier was installed during remediation activities to mitigate the potential for vapor intrusion of residual VOCs --- principally PCE and its degradation products --- from subsurface soil and groundwater into the indoor air of Bay 1. The LUR requires that the vapor barrier not be penetrated, removed, or compromised without prior written approval from SCDHEC. Any renovation, construction, demolition, or alteration activity affecting the floor slab of Bay 1 must include inspection and, if necessary, repair or replacement of the vapor barrier, with prior written notification to SCDHEC.

The LUR is binding upon all current and future owners, tenants, and successors in interest to Lot 7 and constitutes a covenant running with the land enforceable by SCDHEC.

During the site reconnaissance conducted on January 15, 2025, Clearfield observed that the ground floor of Bay 1 is currently occupied by Lowcountry Provisions Inc. as a specialty grocery retailer. This use is consistent with the commercial-use restriction imposed by the LUR. No evidence of vapor barrier damage, slab penetrations, or other conditions suggesting a compromise of the vapor barrier was observed during the site reconnaissance. However, because the vapor barrier is installed beneath the concrete slab, it was not directly visible or inspectable during the reconnaissance. Clearfield recommends that any prospective purchaser confirm the integrity of the vapor barrier through a qualified inspection conducted by a licensed environmental professional prior to or promptly after acquisition, and particularly before any renovation activity affecting the Bay 1 floor slab.

**5.4 Implications for the Subject Property**

The CREC does not constitute a Recognized Environmental Condition because the contamination has been addressed to the satisfaction of SCDHEC and the site has received an NFA letter. However, the CREC classification under ASTM E1527-21 reflects the fact that residual contamination remains in place at levels that exceed unrestricted use standards and that the continued effectiveness of the institutional controls (the recorded LUR) is necessary for the site to remain protective of human health.

If the institutional controls are not maintained --- for example, if the vapor barrier is breached or rendered ineffective during renovation or construction activities, or if the ground floor of Bay 1 is converted to residential use in violation of the LUR --- the NFA status could be jeopardized. Such a breach could result in SCDHEC requiring additional subsurface investigation, remediation measures, or other regulatory action at the expense of the then-current property owner.

The CREC and associated LUR are matters of public record filed with the RMC Office for Charleston County. Clearfield understands from the preliminary title commitment issued for this transaction (Commitment No. PT-2025-04-1178, issued by Prestige Title & Settlement Services LLC) that the LUR recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89 is listed as a Schedule B-II exception to title. Any lender, purchaser, or other party relying on this report should review the recorded LUR in its entirety and consult with legal counsel regarding its implications.

**Note Regarding Planned Renovation:** Clearfield understands from discussions with representatives of Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC that the prospective purchaser intends to undertake a renovation of the Subject Property that may include HVAC system replacement, elevator modernization, and façade restoration. If any renovation activities involve penetration of, alteration to, or work in proximity to the Bay 1 floor slab on Lot 7, care must be taken to avoid compromising the vapor barrier installed beneath the slab. Clearfield recommends that the renovation contractor be made aware of the existence and location of the vapor barrier and of the LUR requirements, and that SCDHEC be notified in writing in advance of any work affecting the Bay 1 slab. Failure to observe these precautions could result in a violation of the LUR and a reopening of the SCDHEC site file, with attendant regulatory and financial consequences for the property owner and, potentially, the lender.

**[6. Phase II Recommendation]{.underline}**

Based on the findings of this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Clearfield does **not** recommend a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (subsurface investigation) for the Subject Property at this time.

The sole environmental finding identified in this assessment --- the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition on Lot 7 --- relates to contamination that has been addressed through SCDHEC-supervised remediation and for which an NFA letter has been issued (August 12, 2021, SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772). Residual contamination is managed through recorded institutional controls in the form of the Land Use Restriction recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89. No conditions were observed during the site reconnaissance or identified during the records review that would suggest a change in subsurface conditions or a failure of the institutional controls. Accordingly, no additional subsurface investigation is warranted at this time unless the institutional controls are breached or new information comes to light suggesting a material change in subsurface conditions.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Clearfield recommends the following actions in connection with the proposed transaction:

> \(a\) The prospective purchaser and borrower (Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC) should obtain and review a complete copy of the SCDHEC remediation file for Site ID SC-29403-0772, including all sampling data, remediation reports, groundwater monitoring results, and the NFA letter with all conditions and attachments.
>
> \(b\) The integrity of the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 floor slab should be confirmed through a qualified inspection by a licensed environmental professional prior to or promptly following acquisition of the Subject Property.
>
> \(c\) Any renovation contractor performing work in or near Bay 1 on Lot 7 should be informed of the existence and location of the vapor barrier and of the requirements of the recorded LUR, and SCDHEC should be notified in writing in advance of any work affecting the Bay 1 floor slab.
>
> \(d\) The lender (Calverley Heritage Bank) should consider requiring the borrower to maintain ongoing compliance with the LUR as a specific covenant in the loan documents, including provisions addressing the consequences of non-compliance and the lender\'s remedies in the event of a breach of the institutional controls.

**Note: Calverley Heritage Bank has waived the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment requirement for this transaction based on the CREC status, the issuance of the SCDHEC NFA letter, and the existence of the recorded institutional controls. This waiver is documented in correspondence dated January 22, 2025, between Marcus Prideaux, Senior Vice President -- Commercial Real Estate Lending, Calverley Heritage Bank, and Clearfield.**

**[7. Conclusions and Opinion]{.underline}**

Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC has performed a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment of the Subject Property located at 520--534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403, in conformance with the scope and limitations of ASTM E1527-21, *Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process*.

The following is a summary of findings:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Condition**                                            **Finding**
  -------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)               None identified

  Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)   One (1) identified --- petroleum and solvent contamination (principally PCE) from former dry cleaning operation at adjacent 518 King Street, migrating to southwest corner of Lot 7; remediated under SCDHEC oversight; NFA letter issued August 12, 2021 (SCDHEC Site ID: SC-29403-0772); subject to recorded Land Use Restriction (Deed Book 1203, Page 89, RMC Office for Charleston County) requiring maintenance of vapor barrier beneath Bay 1 floor slab and prohibiting residential use of ground floor of Lot 7

  Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)   None identified

  De Minimis Conditions                                    None identified

  Significant Data Gaps                                    None identified
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the professional opinion of Clearfield, the Subject Property is suitable for the proposed acquisition and continued commercial use, provided that the institutional controls associated with the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition on Lot 7 are maintained in full compliance with SCDHEC requirements and the terms of the recorded Land Use Restriction. Any future change of use, renovation, or alteration affecting the Bay 1 floor slab on Lot 7 should be undertaken with due regard for the vapor barrier and the LUR, as described in Sections 5 and 6 of this Executive Summary and in greater detail in the full Phase I ESA report.

**[8. Qualifications and Limitations]{.underline}**

This Executive Summary is a condensed extract of the full Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025. The full report, including all appendices --- specifically, Appendix A (Regulatory Database Search Results), Appendix B (Historical Aerial Photographs), Appendix C (Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps), Appendix D (Site Photographs), Appendix E (Interview Records), and Appendix F (Environmental Professional Qualifications) --- should be reviewed in its entirety for a complete understanding of the assessment findings and their basis. This Executive Summary does not replace or supersede the full report.

This assessment was performed for the exclusive use of the identified User (Calverley Heritage Bank) and the additional reliance party (Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC). No other party may rely on this report or this Executive Summary without the prior written consent of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Any unauthorized use or reliance is at the sole risk of the unauthorized party.

The assessment reflects conditions observed and information available as of the date of the site reconnaissance (January 15, 2025) and the date of the report (January 28, 2025). Environmental conditions may change over time due to natural processes, human activities, changes in regulatory standards, or other factors. Clearfield assumes no obligation to update this report and no responsibility for changes in conditions or information that occur after the date of this report.

This assessment involved no invasive investigation, sampling, testing, or analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, or building materials. The conclusions are based solely on non-invasive methods, including visual observation, records review, and interviews. The presence or absence of hazardous substances or petroleum products in environmental media cannot be confirmed without sampling and laboratory analysis.

The findings and conclusions of this assessment are subject to the inherent limitations of the ASTM E1527-21 standard, including limitations associated with the accuracy and completeness of historical records, the reliability of regulatory database information, the scope of visual observations, and the potential for conditions that are not identifiable through non-invasive methods. No Phase I ESA can wholly eliminate uncertainty regarding the potential for recognized environmental conditions in connection with a property.

This assessment was conducted under the supervision and direction of Dr. Rebecca Stanton, P.G., a Licensed Geologist in the State of South Carolina (Registration No. 1847), who serves as a Senior Environmental Scientist and Principal of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Dr. Stanton meets the qualifications of an \"Environmental Professional\" as defined in ASTM E1527-21, Section 3.2.26, and 40 CFR § 312.10, by reason of education, training, and experience in environmental site assessment.

**CERTIFICATION AND SIGNATURE**

I, Dr. Rebecca Stanton, P.G., declare that, to the best of my professional knowledge and belief, I meet the definition of Environmental Professional as defined in § 312.10 of 40 CFR Part 312. I have the specific qualifications based on education, training, and experience to assess a property of the nature, history, and setting of the Subject Property. """Generate a .docx from markdown via Pandoc with an optional reference template.

Usage:
    python generate_from_md.py input.md output.docx [template.docx]

Pandoc applies the template's paragraph and run styles to your markdown.
Best for reports/memos/letters where the template carries firm styling.

Requires pandoc on PATH.
"""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def generate(md_path: Path, output_path: Path, template_path: Path | None = None):
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cmd = ["pandoc", str(md_path), "-o", str(output_path)]
    if template_path is not None:
        cmd.append(f"--reference-doc={template_path}")
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        print(f"pandoc failed: {result.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        print("Usage: generate_from_md.py <input.md> <output.docx> [template.docx]", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    template = Path(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) == 4 else None
    generate(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), template)

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document('build/ref_default.docx')

# --- page setup ---
for s in doc.sections:
    s.top_margin = Inches(1)
    s.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
    s.left_margin = Inches(1)
    s.right_margin = Inches(1)

styles = doc.styles

def setfont(st, name='Times New Roman', size=None, bold=None, italic=None, color=None):
    f = st.font
    f.name = name
    if size: f.size = Pt(size)
    if bold is not None: f.bold = bold
    if italic is not None: f.italic = italic
    if color is not None: f.color.rgb = color
    rpr = st.element.get_or_add_rPr()
    rfonts = rpr.find(qn('w:rFonts'))
    if rfonts is None:
        rfonts = OxmlElement('w:rFonts'); rpr.append(rfonts)
    for a in ('w:ascii','w:hAnsi','w:cs','w:eastAsia'):
        rfonts.set(qn(a), name)

# Body text
for nm in ['Normal','Body Text','First Paragraph','Compact']:
    try:
        st = styles[nm]
    except KeyError:
        continue
    setfont(st, size=11)
    pf = st.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(0)
    pf.space_after = Pt(8)
    pf.line_spacing = 1.08
    pf.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    pf.widow_control = True

# Title
try:
    st = styles['Title']
    setfont(st, size=16, bold=True)
    st.paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
except KeyError:
    pass

# Headings
h1 = styles['Heading 1']; setfont(h1, size=12, bold=True); h1.font.all_caps=False
h1.paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
h1.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(16); h1.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
h1.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

h2 = styles['Heading 2']; setfont(h2, size=11, bold=True)
h2.paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
h2.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(12); h2.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
h2.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

h3 = styles['Heading 3']; setfont(h3, size=11, bold=True, italic=True)
h3.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(10); h3.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
h3.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

# remove heading colors
for h in (h1,h2,h3):
    h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0,0,0)

# Table text style
for nm in ['Table']:
    if nm in [s.name for s in styles]:
        setfont(styles[nm], size=9.5)
        styles[nm].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        styles[nm].paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
        styles[nm].paragraph_format.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT

def add_page_field(par):
    r = par.add_run()
    fld = OxmlElement('w:fldSimple'); fld.set(qn('w:instr'), 'PAGE')
    t = OxmlElement('w:r'); tt = OxmlElement('w:t'); tt.text = '1'
    t.append(tt); fld.append(t)
    par._p.append(fld)
    par.add_run(' of ')
    r2 = par.add_run()
    fld2 = OxmlElement('w:fldSimple'); fld2.set(qn('w:instr'), 'NUMPAGES')
    t2 = OxmlElement('w:r'); tt2 = OxmlElement('w:t'); tt2.text = '1'
    t2.append(tt2); fld2.append(t2)
    par._p.append(fld2)

for s in doc.sections:
    f = s.footer
    p = f.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    add_page_field(p)
    for r in p.runs:
        r.font.size = Pt(9); r.font.name = 'Times New Roman'
    # header
    h = s.header
    hp = h.paragraphs[0]
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    hp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)

doc.save('build/ref.docx')
print('saved')
PYEOF

## ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

### Section 1.1 Definitions

In addition to the terms defined elsewhere in this Mortgage, the following terms have the following meanings when used in this Mortgage. Any capitalized term used but not defined in this Mortgage has the meaning given to it in the Note, and if not defined in the Note, in the Term Sheet.

"**Affiliate**" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly Controls, is Controlled by, or is under common Control with, such Person. "**Control**" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through the ownership of voting interests, by contract or otherwise.

"**Applicable Rate**" means the rate of interest borne by the Loan from time to time as determined under the Note, being a floating rate equal to Daily SOFR plus two hundred eighty-five basis points (2.85%) per annum, subject to a SOFR floor of three percent (3.00%) per annum.

"**Business Day**" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a day on which commercial banks in Savannah, Georgia or Charleston, South Carolina are authorized or required by law to be closed.

"**Completion Guaranty**" means the guaranty of completion described in **Section 5.5(b)** of the Term Sheet, whether contained in the Guaranty or in a separate instrument.

"**CREC**" means the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition identified with respect to Lot 7 in the Phase I ESA, arising from the historical release of perchloroethylene and petroleum-based solvents at the adjoining property located at 518 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, formerly operated as "King Street Cleaners," SCDHEC Site ID No. SC-29403-0772.

"**Daily SOFR**" means the Secured Overnight Financing Rate as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or a successor administrator) on the applicable Business Day, or, if such rate is not published on such Business Day, the rate published on the immediately preceding Business Day, as further defined in the Note.

"**Debt Service**" means, for any period, the sum of (a) all interest accrued and payable on the outstanding principal balance of the Loan during such period at the Applicable Rate (and not at the Default Rate), plus (b) all scheduled principal payments due and payable in respect of the Loan during such period (excluding any balloon, bullet or acceleration payment due on the Maturity Date, and excluding voluntary prepayments and prepayments from casualty, condemnation or other involuntary sources).

"**DSCR**" means, for any Test Period, the ratio of Net Operating Income for such Test Period to Debt Service for such Test Period, expressed as a decimal carried to two decimal places.

"**DSCR Covenant Level**" means 1.25x.

"**Default Rate**" means the per annum rate of interest equal to the Applicable Rate plus five percent (5.00%) per annum, as more particularly set forth in the Note and **Section 13.4**.

"**Environmental Indemnity**" means that certain Environmental Indemnity Agreement of even date herewith executed by Borrower and Guarantor in favor of Lender, as it may be amended, restated or supplemented from time to time.

"**Environmental Laws**" means all federal, state and local statutes, regulations, ordinances, orders, permits and common law requirements relating to pollution, the protection of human health or the environment, or the presence, use, generation, storage, release, threatened release, removal, remediation or disposal of Hazardous Materials, including without limitation CERCLA (42 U.S.C. § 9601 *et seq.*), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (42 U.S.C. § 6901 *et seq.*), the Clean Water Act, the Clean Air Act, the Toxic Substances Control Act, and the South Carolina Hazardous Waste Management Act and the South Carolina Pollution Control Act, together with the regulations promulgated thereunder.

"**Event of Default**" has the meaning given in **Section 13.1**.

"**GC Contract**" means that certain construction contract dated on or about the Closing Date between Borrower, as owner, and Beaufort Builders Group LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company holding South Carolina General Contractor License No. SC-GC-47921, as general contractor (the "**General Contractor**"), providing for a contract sum of Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($2,850,000.00), together with all schedules, exhibits, amendments, change orders and modifications thereto.

"**Guaranty**" means, collectively, the guaranty or guaranties of even date herewith executed by Guarantor in favor of Lender described in **Section 5.5** of the Term Sheet, comprising the Guaranty Agreement, the Completion Guaranty and the Payment Guaranty, whether executed as one or more instruments, as the same may be amended, restated or supplemented from time to time.

"**Hazardous Materials**" means petroleum and petroleum products, perchloroethylene, tetrachloroethylene and all other volatile organic compounds, asbestos, polychlorinated biphenyls, urea formaldehyde, radon, mold, and any other substance, material or waste regulated as hazardous, toxic or a contaminant under any Environmental Laws.

"**Independent Manager**" means a natural person who is not, and has not been within five (5) years prior to appointment, a member, manager, officer, employee, creditor, supplier, customer, contractor, attorney, accountant or affiliate of Borrower, any Member, any Guarantor or any of their respective Affiliates, and who otherwise satisfies the independence requirements described in **Section 8.3**.

"**Initial Advance**" means the initial advance of Loan proceeds in the amount of Twelve Million Five Hundred Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($12,500,000.00), funded on the Closing Date in accordance with the Term Sheet.

"**Leases**" means all present and future leases, subleases, licenses, concessions, occupancy agreements and other agreements (whether written or oral) affecting or demising any portion of the Real Property or the Improvements, including without limitation the Lowcountry Lease, the Harmon & Wren Lease and the Tidemark Lease, together with all guaranties, security agreements, letters of credit, amendments, renewals, extensions and modifications relating thereto.

"**Loan Documents**" means, collectively, the Note, this Mortgage, the assignment of leases, rents and profits contained in **Article IV**, the Environmental Indemnity, the Guaranty, the UCC-1 financing statements (including the fixture filing), the Operating Agreement Amendment, the Reserve Account agreements or acknowledgments required by Lender, and each other document, instrument, certificate or agreement now or hereafter executed and delivered by Borrower, Guarantor or any other Person to or for the benefit of Lender in connection with the Loan, as each may be amended, restated, supplemented, extended, renewed or otherwise modified from time to time.

"**Lowcountry Lease**" means the lease dated December 15, 2022 between Borrower's predecessor in interest, as landlord, and Lowcountry Provisions Inc., a South Carolina corporation, as tenant, demising Bay 1 (approximately 3,800 rentable square feet of ground-floor retail space) at 520 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, for a term expiring December 31, 2027, at a current base rent of $28.50 per rentable square foot per annum ($108,300.00 per annum; $9,025.00 per month), subject to a three percent (3%) annual escalation, and providing for a security deposit of $18,050.00.

"**Harmon & Wren Lease**" means the lease dated June 1, 2021 between Borrower's predecessor in interest, as landlord, and Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company, as tenant, as amended by First Amendment dated September 1, 2023, demising Bay 3 (approximately 3,800 rentable square feet of ground-floor retail space) at 534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, for a term expiring June 30, 2026, at a current base rent of $24.00 per rentable square foot per annum ($91,200.00 per annum; $7,600.00 per month), subject to a two and one-half percent (2.5%) annual escalation, and providing for a security deposit of $15,200.00.

"**Tidemark Lease**" means the lease dated March 15, 2024 between Borrower's predecessor in interest, as landlord, and Tidemark Consulting Group LLC, a Delaware limited liability company registered to do business in South Carolina, as tenant, demising 2nd Floor Suite A (approximately 9,800 rentable square feet of office space) at 520–534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina, for a term expiring March 31, 2029, at a current base rent of $22.00 per rentable square foot per annum ($215,600.00 per annum; $17,966.67 per month), subject to a two and one-half percent (2.5%) annual escalation, and providing for a security deposit of $35,933.00.

"**LUR**" means that certain land use restriction and institutional control recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89 in the RMC Office for Charleston County, South Carolina, imposed by SCDHEC in connection with SCDHEC Site ID No. SC-29403-0772, which restriction (a) prohibits the use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Charleston County Tax Map No. 460-12-04-007, constituting Bay 1, 520 King Street) for residential purposes, and (b) requires the maintenance and periodic inspection of the Vapor Barrier, together with any amendment, modification, extension, replacement or successor instrument, and any related environmental covenant, activity and use limitation or institutional control.

"**Maturity Date**" means April 15, 2030, being the date that is five (5) years after the Closing Date, or such earlier date on which the entire outstanding principal balance of the Loan, together with all accrued and unpaid interest and all other amounts due under the Loan Documents, becomes due and payable, whether by acceleration, prepayment or otherwise.

"**Members**" means Graydon Development Group LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and their respective successors and permitted assigns, and any other Person admitted as a member of Borrower after the Closing Date in accordance with the Operating Agreement and **Article IX**.

"**Net Operating Income**" means, for any Test Period, all gross operating revenues actually received by Borrower from the operation of the Real Property during such Test Period (including base rent, additional rent, expense reimbursements, escalations, percentage rent, parking income, and other income, but excluding (a) security deposits, (b) proceeds of insurance and condemnation awards (other than rent-loss insurance proceeds), (c) interest income, (d) capital contributions and loans, and (e) non-recurring income), less all operating expenses of the Real Property incurred during such Test Period determined in accordance with GAAP on an accrual basis consistently applied, including real property taxes, insurance premiums, utilities, repairs and maintenance, management fees not exceeding four percent (4%) of gross revenues, common area maintenance costs and allocations to a replacement reserve of not less than $0.25 per rentable square foot per annum, but excluding (i) Debt Service, (ii) capital expenditures, (iii) depreciation, amortization and other non-cash items, (iv) income and franchise taxes, (v) expenses attributable to the Renovation (which are capitalized), and (vi) leasing commissions and tenant improvement costs. Net Operating Income shall be subject to adjustment by Lender to normalize (x) non-recurring items, (y) leases at rents below then-prevailing market rent to the extent of any free-rent, abatement or below-market period, and (z) the annualized effect of any Lease executed during the Test Period as though such Lease had been in effect for the entire Test Period.

"**Obligations**" means all present and future debts, obligations and liabilities of Borrower to Lender under or in respect of the Loan Documents, whether direct or indirect, absolute or contingent, due or to become due, now existing or hereafter arising, whether for principal, interest, fees, late charges, prepayment premiums, yield maintenance amounts, costs, expenses, indemnities or otherwise, and including without limitation all future advances made by Lender under this Mortgage, the Renovation Holdback, all Protective Advances, and all interest and other amounts accruing after the commencement of any bankruptcy, insolvency or similar proceeding (whether or not allowed as a claim in such proceeding).

"**Operating Agreement**" means the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of Borrower dated effective as of January 12, 2024, as amended through March 1, 2025, as further amended by the Operating Agreement Amendment and as otherwise amended, restated or supplemented from time to time in accordance with **Section 9.5**.

"**Operating Agreement Amendment**" means an amendment to the Operating Agreement, in form and substance satisfactory to Lender, adding the SPE Provisions, the Independent Manager requirement, the separateness covenants and the unanimity requirement for bankruptcy filings, dissolution, merger and consolidation described in **Article VIII**, executed by all Members and, in the case of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, by its general partner, Tidewater GP Holdings LLC.

"**Payment Guaranty**" means the guaranty of interest shortfall described in **Section 5.5(c)** of the Term Sheet.

"**Permitted Exceptions**" means those exceptions to title listed on **Exhibit B** and approved in writing by Lender, together with any other matter that Lender may hereafter approve in writing in its reasonable discretion.

"**Person**" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, joint venture, trust, association, unincorporated organization, governmental authority or other entity.

"**Phase I ESA**" means that certain Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, Report No. CLR-2025-0119, dated January 28, 2025, prepared by Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC in accordance with ASTM E1527-21.

"**Property**" means the Real Property and the Improvements, collectively.

"**Protective Advance**" means any payment or advance made by Lender pursuant to **Section 14.6**.

"**RMC Office**" means the Office of the Register of Mesne Conveyances for Charleston County, South Carolina.

"**Renovation**" means the renovation, restoration, modernization and improvement of the Improvements contemplated by the Renovation Budget and the GC Contract, comprising HVAC replacement, elevator modernization, façade restoration, tenant improvement allowances, and soft costs and contingency.

"**Renovation Budget**" means the total renovation budget of Three Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($3,150,000.00), comprising the line items and allocations set forth on **Exhibit C**, as the same may be revised only with Lender's prior written approval in accordance with **Section 11.6**.

"**Renovation Holdback**" means the portion of the Loan proceeds in the amount of Two Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($2,250,000.00), being the amount by which the Loan exceeds the Initial Advance, held by Lender and disbursed on a draw basis in accordance with **Article XI**.

"**Reserve Accounts**" means, collectively, the Tax and Insurance Escrow Account, the Capital Replacement Reserve Account and the Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve Account established and maintained with Lender, together with all subaccounts thereof and all sums on deposit therein.

"**SCDHEC**" means the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control.

"**SOFR Floor**" means three percent (3.00%) per annum, as described in **Section 3.6** of the Term Sheet.

"**SPE**" and "**Single-Purpose Entity**" mean a Person that satisfies the requirements of **Article VIII**, including the SPE Provisions.

"**SPE Provisions**" means the single-purpose, separateness, bankruptcy-remoteness and Independent Manager provisions required by **Article VIII** to be contained in the Operating Agreement and in Borrower's certificate of formation.

"**Substantial Completion**" means the completion of all Renovation work in accordance with the approved plans and specifications, as certified by Borrower's architect, and the issuance of a certificate of occupancy (or equivalent) by the City of Charleston for the renovated portions of the Improvements.

"**Substantial Completion Deadline**" means June 15, 2026, being the date that is fourteen (14) months after the Closing Date, as described in **Section 8.3** of the Term Sheet.

"**Tax and Insurance Escrow Account**" has the meaning given in **Section 11.1**.

"**Tenant** means each of Lowcountry Provisions Inc., Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC and Tidemark Consulting Group LLC, and each other Person that hereafter becomes a tenant under a Lease.

"**Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve Account**" has the meaning given in **Section 11.3**.

"**Test Period** means each period of four (4) consecutive fiscal quarters of Borrower (that is, each trailing twelve-month period) ending on the last day of a fiscal quarter of Borrower, commencing with the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2027.

(a) The terms "**Lockout Period**," "**Yield Maintenance Period**," "**Open Prepayment Period**," "**Yield Maintenance Premium**," "**Treasury Rate**" and "**Prepayment Premium**" have the meanings given in **Article XII**.

## ARTICLE II — GRANT OF LIEN; LEGAL DESCRIPTION; FUTURE ADVANCES

### Section 2.1 Lien

Borrower hereby mortgages, grants, bargains, sells, conveys, assigns, transfers and sets over to Lender, and grants to Lender a first-priority lien on and security interest in, the Mortgaged Property, effective as of the Closing Date, as security for the full and punctual payment and performance of the Obligations, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions. This Mortgage is intended to be and shall be construed as a mortgage of real property and a security agreement creating a security interest in personal property and fixtures under the UCC.

### Section 2.2 Legal Description

The Land is more particularly described on **Exhibit A** attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. The Land comprises three (3) contiguous parcels designated as Lots 7, 8 and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, as recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218 in the RMC Office (Charleston County Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008 and 460-12-04-009), together with that certain strip of land formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 and conveyed to Borrower's predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the RMC Office.

### Section 2.3 Future Advances

This Mortgage secures not only the Initial Advance but also the Renovation Holdback and all other present and future advances made by Lender to or for the benefit of Borrower under or in connection with the Loan Documents, whether or not such advances are obligatory on the part of Lender, together with all Protective Advances, and all interest, costs, charges, expenses and other amounts described in **Section 1.1** under the definition of "Obligations." The total amount of the indebtedness secured hereby, exclusive of interest, costs, expenses, indemnities, prepayment premiums, and advances made to protect the Mortgaged Property, is Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($14,750,000.00). Lender shall be entitled to a future advance endorsement to the Title Policy insuring such advances to the extent provided in **Section 5.6** of the Term Sheet.

### Section 2.4 Assignment of Claims and Contracts

Borrower hereby collaterally assigns to Lender, as further security for the Obligations, all of Borrower's right, title and interest in, to and under (a) the GC Contract, including all rights to enforce warranties, retainage rights, liquidated damages, change-order rights and claims thereunder; (b) all architectural, engineering, construction-management and design professional agreements relating to the Renovation; and (c) all warranties, guaranties, surety bonds and indemnities relating to the design, construction or Renovation of the Improvements. Borrower shall deliver to Lender a consent and acknowledgment in form satisfactory to Lender from the General Contractor and each design professional whose agreement is assigned pursuant to this Section, and Borrower shall not amend, waive, terminate or materially modify any such agreement without Lender's prior written consent. Lender's rights under this Section are exercisable only upon and during the continuance of an Event of Default, and prior to such time Borrower may perform its obligations and enforce its rights thereunder in the ordinary course, subject to the terms of this Mortgage.

## ARTICLE III — WARRANTIES OF TITLE; PERMITTED EXCEPTIONS

### Section 3.1 Title Warranties

Borrower represents, warrants and covenants to Lender that: (a) Borrower is the sole fee simple owner of the Real Property, holding good and marketable title thereto, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions; (b) this Mortgage constitutes a valid first-priority lien on and security interest in the Mortgaged Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and no consent, approval or filing (other than the recording and filing contemplated by **Section 16.11**) is required in connection therewith that has not been obtained; (c) Borrower has the full right, power and authority to mortgage, assign and pledge the Mortgaged Property as provided herein; (d) there are no delinquent real property taxes, assessments or governmental charges affecting the Real Property; (e) there are no mechanic's, materialman's or construction liens filed against the Mortgaged Property, and Borrower has not received any notice of intent to file any such lien; and (f) Borrower has not previously mortgaged, assigned or pledged, and shall not mortgage, assign or pledge, any interest in the Mortgaged Property other than to Lender.

### Section 3.2 The Anson Lane Parcel

Without limiting **Section 3.1**, Borrower acknowledges and agrees that: (a) the portion of the Land described as Parcel Two on **Exhibit A** (the vacated Anson Lane strip) was conveyed to Borrower's predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the RMC Office, and Borrower takes such parcel without warranty of title except as set forth in the deed from Hampstead Village Holdings LLC to Borrower; (b) Borrower has caused the Title Insurer to insure fee simple title to Parcel Two in the Title Policy without any Schedule B-II exception that excludes, excepts, qualifies or limits the estate insured as less than fee simple, and Borrower shall deliver at closing either (i) the Title Policy containing no such exception as to Parcel Two, or (ii) an endorsement to the Title Policy (including, at Lender's election, ALTA Endorsement 34 (Identified Exception) or equivalent, or such other affirmative coverage as Lender may reasonably require) affirmatively insuring over any such exception, in each case at Borrower's sole expense; (c) Borrower shall, upon Lender's request, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from the City of Charleston such confirmatory instruments, quitclaim deeds or ordinances as may be necessary to permit the Title Insurer to continue such coverage; and (d) Borrower shall not grant, release or relinquish any right of access, loading or parking over or across Parcel Two without Lender's prior written consent. The total amount of the indebtedness secured hereby, exclusive of interest, costs, expenses, indemnities, prepayment premiums, and advances made to protect the Mortgaged Property, is Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand and No/100 Dollars ($14,750,000.00). Lender shall be entitled to a future advance endorsement to the Title Policy insuring such advances to the extent provided in **Section 5.6** of the Term Sheet.

### Section 2.4 Assignment of Claims and Contracts

Borrower hereby collaterally assigns to Lender, as further security for the Obligations, all of Borrower's right, title and interest in, to and under (a) the GC Contract, including all rights to enforce warranties, retainage rights, liquidated damages, change-order rights and claims thereunder; (b) all architectural, engineering, construction-management and design professional agreements relating to the Renovation; and (c) all warranties, guaranties, surety bonds and indemnities relating to the design, construction or Renovation of the Improvements. Borrower shall deliver to Lender a consent and acknowledgment in form satisfactory to Lender from the General Contractor and each design professional whose agreement is assigned pursuant to this Section, and Borrower shall not amend, waive, terminate or materially modify any such agreement without Lender's prior written consent. Lender's rights under this Section are exercisable only upon and during the continuance of an Event of Default, and prior to such time Borrower may perform its obligations and enforce its rights thereunder in the ordinary course, subject to the terms of this Mortgage.

## ARTICLE III — WARRANTIES OF TITLE; PERMITTED EXCEPTIONS

### Section 3.1 Title Warranties

Borrower represents, warrants and covenants to Lender that: (a) Borrower is the sole fee simple owner of the Real Property, holding good and marketable title thereto, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions; (b) this Mortgage constitutes a valid first-priority lien on and security interest in the Mortgaged Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, and no consent, approval or filing (other than the recording and filing contemplated by **Section 16.11**) is required in connection therewith that has not been obtained; (c) Borrower has the full right, power and authority to mortgage, assign and pledge the Mortgaged Property as provided herein; (d) there are no delinquent real property taxes, assessments or governmental charges affecting the Real Property; (e) there are no mechanic's, materialman's or construction liens filed against the Mortgaged Property, and Borrower has not received any notice of intent to file any such lien; and (f) Borrower has not previously mortgaged, assigned or pledged, and shall not mortgage, assign or pledge, any interest in the Mortgaged Property other than to Lender.

### Section 3.2 The Anson Lane Parcel

Without limiting **Section 3.1**, Borrower acknowledges and agrees that: (a) the portion of the Land described as Parcel Two on **Exhibit A** (the vacated Anson Lane strip) was conveyed to Borrower's predecessor in title by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the RMC Office, and Borrower takes such parcel without warranty of title except as set forth in the deed from Hampstead Village Holdings LLC to Borrower; (b) Borrower has caused the Title Insurer to insure fee simple title to Parcel Two in the Title Policy without any Schedule B-II exception that excludes, excepts, qualifies or limits the estate insured as less than fee simple, and Borrower shall deliver at closing either (i) the Title Policy containing no such exception as to Parcel Two, or (ii) an endorsement to the Title Policy (including, at Lender's election, ALTA Endorsement 34 (Identified Exception) or equivalent, or such other affirmative coverage as Lender may reasonably require) affirmatively insuring over any such exception, in each case at Borrower's sole expense; (c) Borrower shall, upon Lender's request, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from the City of Charleston such confirmatory instruments, quitclaim deeds or ordinances as may be necessary to permit the Title Insurer to continue such coverage; and (d) Borrower shall not grant, release or relinquish any right of access, loading or parking over or across Parcel Two without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower's failure to satisfy the requirements of clause (b) of this Section as of the Closing Date shall constitute a failure of a condition precedent to Lender's obligation to fund the Initial Advance under **Section 12.1(b)** of the Term Sheet, unless waived by Lender in writing.

### Section 3.3 Balcony Encroachment

Lender acknowledges that a decorative iron balcony extends approximately two and one-half (2.5) feet beyond the front façade of the Improvements over and across the King Street public right-of-way, as shown on the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Cartwright Land Surveying LLC dated January 15, 2025 and as described in Exception 5 of Schedule B, Part II of the Title Commitment. Borrower represents and warrants that, to Borrower's knowledge, no governmental authority has asserted that such encroachment constitutes a violation of law or has required its removal. Borrower covenants that it shall (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and maintain in effect, within ninety (90) days after the Closing Date, a valid encroachment license, permit or other authorization from the City of Charleston for the balcony, and shall deliver a copy thereof to Lender upon receipt; (b) procure at closing, at Borrower's expense, a survey/encroachment endorsement to the Title Policy (ALTA Endorsement 28.1 or equivalent) if available from the Title Insurer on commercially reasonable terms; (c) include the balcony repair and stabilization within the scope of the façade restoration line item of the Renovation Budget; and (d) not remove, alter or materially modify the balcony without Lender's prior written consent, except to the extent required by any governmental authority, in which case Borrower shall give Lender at least five (5) Business Days' prior written notice (or such shorter notice as is practicable) and shall promptly furnish copies of all related notices, permits and orders to Lender.

Borrower represents, warrants and covenants to Lender that: (a) Borrower has received and reviewed a copy of the Phase I ESA and the recorded LUR; (b) other than the CREC and the LUR, there are no Recognized Environmental Conditions, Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions, Hazardous Materials, underground or above-ground storage tanks, or violations of Environmental Laws affecting the Property; (c) the current use of Bay 1 as a specialty grocery is consistent with the LUR; (d) Borrower has delivered to Lender a complete copy of the SCDHEC file for Site ID No. SC-29403-0772 (including the No Further Action determination dated August 12, 2021, with all conditions and attachments), or shall deliver the same within ten (10) Business Days after the Closing Date; and (e) Borrower is not aware of any pending or threatened notice, claim, order or proceeding by SCDHEC or any other governmental authority alleging noncompliance with the LUR or otherwise relating to the CREC.

### Section 3.5 No Reliance on Lender

Borrower acknowledges that Lender has made no representation or warranty to Borrower regarding the physical, environmental, structural, title or economic condition of the Property, the existence or sufficiency of the LUR, the integrity of the Vapor Barrier, the sufficiency of the Renovation Budget, or the availability of any encroachment license for the balcony, and that Borrower has made its own independent investigation thereof.

## ARTICLE IV — ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT OF LEASES, RENTS AND PROFITS

### Section 4.1 Absolute and Present Assignment

For value received, and as additional security for the Obligations, Borrower hereby **unconditionally, absolutely and presently** grants, bargains, sells, conveys, transfers, assigns and sets over to Lender all of Borrower's right, title and interest, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, in and to: (a) all Leases, including the Lowcountry Lease, the Harmon & Wren Lease and the Tidemark Lease, and all extensions, renewals, amendments, replacements and substitutions thereof and all new Leases hereafter entered into; (b) all rents, issues, profits, revenues, income, receipts and other sums of every kind now or hereafter due or payable under or in respect of the Leases or the use or occupancy of the Property, including base rent, additional rent, percentage rent, expense and tax reimbursements, escalations, parking and other revenues, and all sums paid or payable on account of any Lease termination, surrender, buy-out or settlement; (c) all security deposits, prepaid rent, letters of credit and other collateral held in connection with the Leases; (d) all guaranties of the Leases and all rights and remedies of Borrower thereunder; and (e) all proceeds of the foregoing. This assignment is intended to be, and shall be construed as, an absolute and present assignment of the Leases and Rents and not merely a collateral assignment or an assignment as additional security.

### Section 4.2 Statutory Acknowledgment; Perfection and Enforcement

The parties intend that this **Article IV** constitute an assignment of rents within the meaning of the Uniform Assignment of Rents Act as enacted in the State of South Carolina (the "**UARAA**"), and that all of the rights and remedies afforded to an assignee thereunder be available to Lender. ### Section 4.3 License to Borrower to Collect Rents

Notwithstanding **Sections 4.1** and **4.2**, Lender grants to Borrower a revocable license to collect, and to retain and use, the Rents in the ordinary course of business until the occurrence of an Event of Default. Such license is automatically revoked, without further notice or action, upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, and Lender may thereupon exercise any and all rights and remedies under this **Article IV**, at law or in equity, including the right to notify Tenants to pay Rents directly to Lender. Borrower shall, promptly upon Lender's written request (and in any event within five (5) Business Days), execute and deliver to each Tenant a notice in form satisfactory to Lender directing such Tenant to pay all Rents directly to Lender or its designee; Borrower hereby irrevocably appoints Lender as its attorney-in-fact for the limited purpose of executing and delivering such notices if Borrower fails to do so.

### Section 4.4 Notice to Tenants

Any Tenant who makes payment to Lender in accordance with such notice shall be discharged from any further obligation to Borrower with respect to such payment.

### Section 4.5 Borrower's Warranties Regarding Leases

Borrower represents, warrants and covenants that: (a) the rent roll delivered to Lender and attached as **Exhibit D** is true, correct and complete as of the Closing Date; (b) Borrower has good right, full power and lawful authority to absolutely assign the Leases and the Rents, including without limitation the Lowcountry Lease, notwithstanding the absence of any assignment, subletting or consent-to-assignment provision in the Lowcountry Lease, and Borrower has not previously assigned, pledged or encumbered the Leases or the Rents; (c) each Lease is in full force and effect and, to Borrower's knowledge, no default or event of default exists thereunder on the part of landlord or tenant, and no Tenant has asserted any offset, defense, claim in recoupment or withholding right; (d) Borrower has delivered to Lender true and complete copies of each Lease, together with all amendments, guaranties and side letters; (e) no Lease contains any option to purchase, right of first refusal to purchase, or other right in favor of any Tenant to acquire any interest in the Property, other than the right of first refusal in favor of Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to the leasing of Bay 2 (approximately 3,800 rentable square feet) as set forth in the Harmon & Wren Lease, which is a right to lease only and not a right to purchase; (f) no Rents have been collected in advance of the current month other than as disclosed in **Exhibit D**, and all security deposits held under the Leases are as set forth in **Exhibit D** ($69,183.00 in the aggregate) and are held by Borrower and shall be maintained in accordance with applicable law; and (g) Borrower has not received any notice from any Tenant of any intention to terminate, surrender, vacate or materially reduce its leased premises, other than the renewal and termination rights disclosed in **Exhibit D**.

### Section 4.6 Payment of Taxes; No Liability of Lender

Borrower shall pay, before delinquency, all real property taxes, assessments and governmental charges levied against the Property. Lender shall not be liable for, and shall not have any obligation with respect to, the performance of any obligation of landlord under any Lease, and Borrower shall indemnify and hold Lender harmless from and against all claims, liabilities, losses, damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) asserted against Lender arising out of any Lease or out of Lender's exercise of its rights under this **Article IV**, except to the extent arising from Lender's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Borrower's obligations under the Leases shall not be deemed to have been assumed by Lender by reason of this assignment.

### Section 4.7 Estoppel Certificates; Subordination and Non-Disturbance Agreements

(a) Borrower shall deliver to Lender, within ten (10) Business Days after Lender's written request (and in any event not less frequently than annually), a current rent roll and a certification as to the status of each Lease, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause each Tenant to execute and deliver to Lender a tenant estoppel certificate in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender. Borrower acknowledges that the delivery of estoppel certificates from each of the three (3) Tenants in occupancy as of the Closing Date is a condition precedent to the Initial Advance under **Section 12.1(j)** of the Term Sheet, and that Lender does not intend to waive such condition with respect to the Lowcountry Lease.

(b) Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause each Tenant to execute and deliver a subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreement ("**SNDA**") in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender, it being acknowledged that the delivery of executed SNDAs from each of the three (3) Tenants in occupancy is a condition precedent to the Initial Advance under **Section 12.1(k)** of the Term Sheet. Borrower shall deliver an SNDA from each Tenant which hereafter enters into a Lease concurrently with the execution of such Lease.

(c) Without limiting the foregoing, within ninety (90) days after the Closing Date Borrower shall deliver to Lender a tenant estoppel certificate executed by Lowcountry Provisions Inc. in form reasonably satisfactory to Lender that (i) acknowledges the existence of this Mortgage and the assignment of the Leases and Rents to Lender, (ii) confirms the material terms of the Lowcountry Lease, and (iii) agrees that, upon written notice from Lender following an Event of Default, the Tenant shall pay all Rents directly to Lender. Borrower shall further use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, at the next renewal, extension or amendment of the Lowcountry Lease (and, if earlier, upon Lender's request following an Event of Default), an amendment to the Lowcountry Lease adding a customary assignment and consent-to-assignment provision, and Borrower shall promptly deliver copies of all correspondence and executed documentation to Lender.

### Section 4.8 Leasing Restrictions

Borrower shall not, without Lender's prior written consent (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), enter into, amend, renew, extend, terminate, accept a surrender of, or waive any material right under, any Lease (a) demising more than five thousand (5,000) rentable square feet, or (b) having a term (including renewal options) exceeding five (5) years. Borrower shall not enter into any Lease containing any option to purchase, right of first refusal to purchase, or right of first offer to purchase any interest in the Property, or any provision permitting the Tenant to sublease or assign without Lender's consent. All Leases shall be on commercially reasonable terms consistent with prevailing market terms for comparable mixed-use commercial properties in the Charleston, South Carolina metropolitan area. Borrower shall cause each Lease to provide that it is subordinate to this Mortgage, subject to Lender's delivery of a commercially reasonable SNDA. Borrower shall not lease any portion of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1) for residential use, or permit any change in the use of Bay 1 that would violate the LUR.

### Section 4.9 Right of First Refusal — Bay 2

Borrower shall comply with, and shall not circumvent, the right of first refusal in favor of Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to Bay 2 as set forth in the Harmon & Wren Lease. Borrower shall deliver to Lender copies of any bona fide third-party offer for Bay 2 and any ROFR notice delivered or received. Borrower acknowledges that the exercise or waiver of such right of first refusal may extend the lease-up period for Bay 2 and that Lender has taken no position on the enforceability or scope of such right.
